candidates.attacker_control: The HTTP Content-Type header of a POST. It must contain the literal 'multipart/form-data' to satisfy Dispatcher.wrapRequest's content_type.contains(...) check (Dispatcher.java:792) while not starting with 'multipart/' so that Commons FileUpload's parseRequest rejects it with InvalidContentTypeException, whose message repeats the header value. The header can therefore carry an OGNL payload such as %{(...)} together with the literal 'multipart/form-data'.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified that struts-messages.properties (34-36) and its locale copies define no key for InvalidContentTypeException, so findDefaultText returns null and the attacker message is used as the fallback (LocalizedTextUtil 719-733). Verified ActionContext exists at wrapping time (StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter 91-94; PrepareOperations.createActionContext 71-91 creates an OgnlValueStack and puts the container into its context via OgnlValueStackFactory 62-67), so the sink is reachable during request wrapping, before any action runs. Verified TextParser is bound to OgnlTextParser (struts-default.xml:130) and that evaluation ultimately goes through OgnlUtil.getValue/Ognl.getValue with the stack's OgnlContext carrying SecurityMemberAccess (OgnlValueStack 88-97), so the sandbox - not removing the evaluation - is the only mitigating layer. Also noted that JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage (236-247, 510-514) and MultiPartRequestWrapper.buildErrorMessage (84-109) contain the same pattern; these are treated as the same root cause, not separate candidates.
candidates.impact: Untrusted header text is executed as an OGNL expression in the request's ValueStack context. The expression can read/modify objects reachable from the stack and OGNL context (action properties, #context, parameter/session/request maps, DI container entry placed in the stack context by OgnlValueStackFactory.createValueStack lines 62-67) and, subject to the OGNL member-access rules, invoke methods/static access. Guards are present in this snapshot (struts.excludedPackageNames=java.lang,ognl,javax, struts.excludedClasses=com.opensymphony.xwork2.ActionContext, allowStaticMethodAccess=false, OGNL 3.1.2), which is why the report is framed as expression injection with possible RCE rather than a proven command execution; this exact code shape (multipart error message evaluated as OGNL) is the pattern of a known unauthenticated RCE in Struts.
candidates.prerequisites: Application uses the standard Struts filter chain (StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter or StrutsPrepareFilter) with default settings so that prepare.createActionContext() runs before prepare.wrapRequest() (filter lines 91-94), the default multipart parser 'jakarta' is used (default.properties:69), the request URL is not excluded, and commons-fileupload (1.3.1 declared in the root pom) builds its InvalidContentTypeException message from the request Content-Type. The upload error key must be absent from the configured bundles for the attacker string to be used as fallback (verified: struts-messages.properties only defines SizeLimitExceededException and IOException).
candidates.root_cause: JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage() passes the Commons FileUpload exception's message as the defaultMessage argument to LocalizedTextUtil.findText(). Because no bundle entry exists for the exception key, LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage() uses that attacker-influenced string and runs it through TextParseUtil.translateVariables() -> OgnlTextParser.evaluate() -> ValueStack.findValue() -> OgnlUtil.getValue(), i.e. it is parsed and executed as OGNL. The Content-Type header value is reproduced inside the file-upload exception message, so %{...}/${...} sequences placed in that header are evaluated against the request's ActionContext/ValueStack without any escaping or evaluation suppression on the fallback path.
candidates.title: Attacker-controlled multipart Content-Type is evaluated as an OGNL expression via the localized upload-error path
candidates.trace: StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter.doFilter -> PrepareOperations.createActionContext (ActionContext+OgnlValueStack created) -> PrepareOperations.wrapRequest -> Dispatcher.wrapRequest (line 792 'contains multipart/form-data') -> new MultiPartRequestWrapper -> JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse (82-107) -> parseRequest/ServletFileUpload.parseRequest -> FileUploadException whose message embeds Content-Type -> buildErrorMessage (115-119) -> LocalizedTextUtil.findText (391-393 -> 448-593; no bundle hit, fallback branch 570-573) -> getDefaultMessage (729 TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack)) -> OgnlTextParser.evaluate (49 evaluator.evaluate(var)) -> OgnlValueStack.findValue(expr, String.class) (366-368) -> OgnlUtil.getValue -> Ognl.getValue with the stack's OgnlContext.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed and no HTTP request was sent. The exact wording of the commons-fileupload exception (external dependency, not in the tree) and whether the OGNL 3.1.2 / SecurityMemberAccess combination in this snapshot can be fully bypassed for command execution were not runtime-verified; the candidate is a source-evidence lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
candidates.weakness_type: Expression-language injection of untrusted request data (OGNL) - CWE-917 / CWE-94

coverage_summary: Direct source reading was used for the core paths that form the candidate: dispatcher/filter/wrapper (StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter, StrutsPrepareFilter, PrepareOperations, Dispatcher, MultiPartRequestWrapper), multipart parsers (JakartaMultiPartRequest, JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest), localization and expression evaluation (LocalizedTextUtil, TextParseUtil, OgnlTextParser, OgnlValueStack, OgnlValueStackFactory, OgnlUtil, SecurityMemberAccess), action mapping/method security (DefaultActionMapper, ActionConfig/AllowedMethods, DefaultActionProxy, XmlConfigurationProvider), plus configuration and bundles (struts-default.xml, default.properties, struts-messages*.properties) and spot checks in the REST plugin and showcase apps. The P1 relation index is explicitly partial: 3620 visible files, 1954 Java files, only 33 parsed, 524 omitted, 24 parse errors, no control/data-flow or semantic resolution, and its facts/edges are navigation hints only - they were not treated as findings. I did not exhaustively read all 1567 core files, 829 plugin files, the apps/archetypes/bundles trees, or third-party jars not present in the tree.
limitations: No code was compiled or executed, no HTTP traffic was generated, and no dependency jar (commons-fileupload, OGNL) source is present in the tree; the external library's exception text and OGNL runtime behavior are inferred from the call sites and advertised versions (commons-fileupload 1.3.1, ognl 3.1.2).

The P1 index coverage is partial (33 parsed files reported, 524 omitted, 24 parse errors) and offers no data-flow/reachability proof; every relation used here was re-verified in source text, but areas not read directly remain uninspected.

Whether the OGNL member-access layer (SecurityMemberAccess with allowStaticMethodAccess=false, excluded packages java.lang,ognl,javax) fully blocks command execution in this snapshot was not verifiable locally; therefore the impact statement distinguishes expression evaluation (certain) from RCE (conditional).

The snapshot's exact upstream commit/date could not be established from inside the tree (no VCS metadata, changelog or version bump); only the 2.5-SNAPSHOT version and WW-45xx references are visible, which is why the finding is reported as a candidate lead rather than a confirmed unfixed vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Unconfigured XStream deserialization in the REST plugin (XStreamHandler.createXStream() returns new XStream(); toObject calls xstream.fromXML(in, target); plugins/rest/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/rest/handler/XStreamHandler.java:43-50)
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible deserialization issue, but requires the REST plugin, an XML Content-Type mapped to this handler and a suitable gadget on the classpath, and no specific unvalidated-data-to-sink transition could be confirmed inside the tree; weaker and more conditional than the core multipart/OGNL path.

The '!'-DMI branch is gated by allowDynamicMethodCalls (default false), the WW-4589 guard prevents overriding an explicit method, and strict-method-invocation/allowed-methods checks exist in DefaultActionProxy (197-201); no concrete bypass was established from source.

rejected_leads.lead: DMI through the default mapper (method:/action: parameter prefixes, DefaultActionMapper.java:115-215)
rejected_leads.reason: Both prefixes are gated by allowDynamicMethodCalls, which defaults to false (default.properties:109) and is only enabled by explicit configuration, so no vulnerable default exists.

rejected_leads.lead: SQL string construction in the bundled showcase app (e.g. apps/showcase AbstractDao/EmployeeDao/TestDataProvider, index-flagged 'injection' facts)
rejected_leads.reason: Demo/sample application code, not the framework attack surface, and the flagged sites are ordinary concatenated queries in example DAOs; not selected.

summary: Source review of an Apache Struts 2.5-SNAPSHOT tree (3620 model-visible files, mostly core/plugins/apps). The strongest evidence-backed issue is an expression-injection sink in the default multipart path: the parser's exception message, which embeds the attacker-supplied Content-Type header, is passed as the default message into LocalizedTextUtil.findText and then executed as OGNL (%{...}/${...}) with TextParseUtil/OgnlTextParser against the request's ValueStack. All links of the chain (default parser 'jakarta', filter ordering so ActionContext/ValueStack exists during multipart wrapping, missing resource-bundle key forcing the fallback message, OGNL evaluation helper) were verified directly in source. Impact is expression evaluation of untrusted header data with historical RCE precedent for this exact code shape; full RCE depends on OGNL/SecurityMemberAccess behavior I could not execute. One candidate is submitted; other plausible leads (unconfigured XStream in the REST plugin, REST/DMI method handling) are listed as rejected/unconfirmed.
